verifier: blind Claude agent re-implementation from the brief only; comparison computed by compare_independent.py (agent verification, not human)
ambiguities: Output rows exist for every match (usable or not); usability only governs which matches enter history. A row is NaN only if its inputs (sp/rr of either player, t) are NaN.
Rows with null tourney_date/winner_id/loser_id dropped before computing k and output; rows kept in concatenated sorted-file order.
Window: history day < d and day >= d-1095 using calendar-day differences of YYYYMMDD dates; weight exponent uses integer day difference/365.
t pooled over both players' rows = sum of both sides' (1stWon+2ndWon) / sum of both svpt over usable same-tour matches in window.
Sets: v1 = e2 - e1^2 using e1,e2 already averaged over the two first-server cases (not average of per-case variances).
Tiebreak recursion evaluated only on x,y<=6 with terminal 7-<=5 (win by two never reaches 7-6); at 6-6 the closed form a/(a+b) is used.
Tiebreak when B serves the set's first point: A wins with 1 - f computed with S1=B (pS1=pB, pS2=pA).
best_of coerced to numeric; best_of==5 uses 5-set law, everything else (3, null, other) uses the 2/3-set law.
gps_p_tiebreak_pre equals P(13) since 6-6 always leads to 7-6/6-7.
A set is terminal at 6-x (x<=4) or 7-5 per brief; 6-5 continues, 6-6 goes to tiebreak.
